issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to place the computed pixel memory address in EDI and to read the pixel with "mov ecx, [edi]" (part a), but the template and the provided solution compute and expect the address in ESI and read with "mov ecx, [esi]". This register mismatch (EDI vs ESI) is a cross-artifact inconsistency: following the problem text will make the student's code inconsistent with the template's calling/usage convention and with the reference solution, causing incorrect behavior or confusing debugging.
issues.suggested_fix: Make register usage consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to instruct students to place the computed address in ESI and to use "mov ecx, [esi]" (preferred, since template and solution already use ESI), or (B) modify the template and solution to use EDI everywhere (compute address into EDI and load with "mov ecx, [edi]"). Update the problem text or code comments accordingly so all references use the same register name.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to place the computed pixel memory address in register EDI and then read the pixel with 'mov ecx, [edi]'. The template and the provided solution, however, expect/use ESI as the register holding the computed address (comments and code compute the address into ESI and use '[esi]'). This mismatch (EDI vs ESI) refers to the same conceptual entity — the computed pixel memory address — with different identifiers across artifacts and will confuse students about which register they must produce/inspect.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the register usage consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to ESI (change 'Ergebnis nach EDI' and 'mov ecx, [edi]' to 'Ergebnis nach ESI' and 'mov ecx, [esi]') or change the template/solution to use EDI consistently. The simplest fix: edit the problem text to require the result in ESI and to use 'mov ecx, [esi]' so it matches the template comments and solution code.
